notes: 503A compounding-pharmacy letter framed around loss of the section 503A exemption (no valid prescriptions for individually-identified patients for some sterile products, e.g. Lidocaine/Tetracaine/Phenylephrine Gel and Dutasteride Injectable), with adulteration charged under 501(a)(2)(A) insanitary conditions (dirty ISO 5/ISO 7 surfaces, detected microbial contamination in critical areas, poor aseptic technique) rather than a standard 21 CFR 211 CGMP citation, so CGMP is omitted from violation_categories (the letter only discusses CGMP as a future/conditional obligation, not a current specific-section finding). Also charges misbranding (502(f)(1), no adequate directions for use) and unapproved new drug (505(a)/301(d)). contamination_present is true (actual microbial contamination detected in the ISO 5 area) and recall_concern is true (FDA acknowledges the firm's voluntary recall of all sterile compounded products).
